question.problem:
Consider the functions $y(x)=Ax$ and $f(y)=By,$ where $x\in {R}^{3},y\in {R}^{2},$ and the matrices $A$ and $B$ are given by $$ A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]. $$ What is $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x))$ evaluated at ${x}_{0}=[0,\,-1,\,1]^{T}?$
${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x))|}_{{x}_{0}}=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
$6$ {{field-4}} $3$
question.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x))=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

- The function $f$ acts on a vector $y\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $B$ and outputs a vector $f(y)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}y}=B.
$$

- The function $y$ acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{3}$ by multiplying it by $A$ and outputs a vector $y(x)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=A.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x)) & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \\  & =BA \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -7 & 9 \\ 6 & 9 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
